title: Only 12% Of Adults Can Pass This Flight Attendant Entrance Exam
summary: Explore cabin safety and service through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Ready for the next challenge?
Think safety, service and teamwork.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of cabin safety and service. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official airline recruitment, safety, medical or employment assessment. Procedures and commands vary by aircraft, airline and jurisdiction.

next.tagline: Up next: Responding to the unexpected.
Up next: Support for every passenger.
Up next: Flight and weather basics.

insights.overview: Your cabin crew score at a glance

flightattendant-s1q1.question: Why should cabin baggage be correctly stowed?

answers.a1: To increase the number of exits
answers.a2: To reduce obstruction and the risk of moving objects
answers.a4: To replace seat restraints

flightattendant-s1q2.question: Why must aisles and exit areas stay clear?

answers.a1: People may need to move through them promptly
answers.a2: It changes the aircraft’s magnetic heading
answers.a4: It removes the need for cabin checks

flightattendant-s1q3.question: What is the purpose of the passenger safety briefing?

answers.a1: To replace every crew instruction later
answers.a2: To explain important safety information for that aircraft and flight
answers.a3: To guarantee there will be no turbulence
answers.a4: To advertise only the destination

flightattendant-s1q4.question: Why does a passenger’s seat belt remain useful while seated?

answers.a1: It makes baggage weight irrelevant
answers.a2: It controls cabin temperature
answers.a4: Unexpected turbulence can occur

flightattendant-s1q5.question: A loose object is found in the aisle. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a1: Leave it because it is small
answers.a2: Move it into an exit path
answers.a3: Have it safely secured according to the crew procedure
answers.a4: Ask passengers to step over it all flight

flightattendant-s1q6.question: Why should safety equipment locations be familiar to the crew?

answers.a1: So all equipment can be used interchangeably
answers.a2: So the appropriate equipment can be found promptly
answers.a3: So equipment checks can be skipped
answers.a4: So training becomes unnecessary

flightattendant-s1q7.question: A passenger has not understood a safety instruction. What helps?

answers.a1: Explain it clearly and check understanding
answers.a2: Repeat only unfamiliar abbreviations
answers.a3: Ignore the issue if the cabin is busy
answers.a4: Assume a nod is enough in every case

flightattendant-s2q1.question: A passenger says a meal conflicts with a stated allergy. What is the best response?

answers.a1: Promise it is safe without checking
answers.a2: Check reliable ingredient information and the applicable service procedure
answers.a4: Remove a visible ingredient and guarantee safety

flightattendant-s2q2.question: Two passengers want the same available item. What supports fair service?

answers.a1: Pretend the request was not heard
answers.a2: Promise both the same single item
answers.a3: Apply the service policy consistently and explain alternatives
answers.a4: Choose according to appearance

flightattendant-s2q3.question: A passenger is upset about a delay. What is a useful opening?

answers.a1: Acknowledge the concern and share verified information
answers.a2: Invent an arrival time
answers.a4: Blame another passenger

flightattendant-s2q4.question: A drink spills into an aisle. What should be addressed first?

answers.a1: The immediate slip hazard using the appropriate procedure
answers.a2: Only the colour of the carpet
answers.a3: The order of the refreshments menu
answers.a4: Whether anyone has taken a photograph

flightattendant-s2q5.question: A passenger requests something you cannot provide. What is helpful?

answers.a1: Promise it anyway
answers.a2: Ignore all further requests
answers.a3: Make up a rule to end the conversation
answers.a4: Explain the limit politely and offer a suitable alternative if available

flightattendant-s2q6.question: Why keep service items secure when they are not being used?

answers.a1: It makes them permanently sterile
answers.a2: It changes the aircraft’s altitude
answers.a3: They can move and cause injury or obstruction
answers.a4: It replaces checking the cabin

flightattendant-s2q7.question: Which message avoids an unsupported promise?

answers.a1: “Every connection is guaranteed”
answers.a2: “I will check what options are available”
answers.a4: “There is never any risk”

flightattendant-s3q1.question: What does cabin pressurisation help provide at high altitude?

answers.a1: A replacement for the aircraft structure
answers.a2: An unlimited oxygen supply in every situation
answers.a4: An environment in which people can breathe more comfortably

flightattendant-s3q2.question: What is the purpose of emergency lighting in the cabin?

answers.a1: To help people find routes and exits when needed
answers.a2: To change the outside wind
answers.a4: To replace crew training

flightattendant-s3q3.question: What does a smoke detector do?

answers.a1: Detects conditions associated with smoke and gives a warning
answers.a2: Automatically proves the source of every smell
answers.a4: Removes all smoke instantly

flightattendant-s3q4.question: Why are different fire extinguishers not automatically interchangeable?

answers.a1: Their colour alone determines every use worldwide
answers.a2: They may be designed for different hazards and uses
answers.a4: Any extinguisher removes all need for training

flightattendant-s3q5.question: What is a galley on an aircraft?

answers.a1: The pilot’s instrument panel
answers.a2: The outside wing surface
answers.a4: The area used for food and drink preparation

answers.a1: The aircraft’s tail cone
answers.a2: The passenger baggage shelf
answers.a4: The area where the pilots control the aircraft

flightattendant-s3q7.question: Why follow the specific aircraft’s equipment instructions?

answers.a1: Every aircraft uses identical equipment
answers.a2: Equipment labels are decorative only
answers.a3: Designs and operating procedures can differ
answers.a4: General guesses are always sufficient

flightattendant-s4q1.question: An important instruction is unclear. What is the best response?

answers.a1: Assume another team’s instruction applies
answers.a2: Ignore every later message
answers.a4: Guess from one familiar word

flightattendant-s4q2.question: What is the purpose of reading back a critical instruction?

answers.a1: To transfer all responsibility to the sender
answers.a2: To make the message longer for its own sake
answers.a3: To replace carrying out the confirmed instruction
answers.a4: To let the sender check that it was understood correctly

flightattendant-s4q3.question: Two tasks require the same person at the same time. What should be clarified?

answers.a1: Which task has the shorter name
answers.a2: Only the colour of the checklist
answers.a4: Nothing; the conflict resolves itself

answers.a1: Relevant facts, unresolved concerns and the next required actions
answers.a2: Only the person’s first name
answers.a4: Only a reassurance that everything is fine

flightattendant-s4q5.question: A colleague reports a new safety concern. What supports effective teamwork?

answers.a1: Hide it to protect the schedule
answers.a2: Dismiss it because the colleague is junior
answers.a4: Listen, clarify and address the concern

flightattendant-s4q6.question: A procedure changes. Which document should guide the task?

answers.a1: A remembered version from another organisation
answers.a2: The current authorised procedure
answers.a4: Any older copy that looks familiar

flightattendant-s4q7.question: Why assign a clear owner to a follow-up action?

answers.a1: So no record is needed
answers.a2: So the action becomes automatically complete
answers.a3: So responsibility and completion can be tracked
answers.a4: So nobody else may raise concerns

flightattendant-s5q1.question: A passenger reports smoke in the cabin. What is the appropriate initial response?

answers.a1: Open a random equipment panel
answers.a2: Wait to see whether another passenger mentions it
answers.a3: Notify the crew promptly and follow the emergency procedure
answers.a4: Assume every smell is harmless

flightattendant-s5q2.question: During an emergency, which instructions should passengers follow?

answers.a1: The crew’s current safety instructions
answers.a2: Instructions from an unrelated aircraft video
answers.a3: Unverified advice shouted by another passenger
answers.a4: Only the original boarding announcement

flightattendant-s5q3.question: Why should emergency commands be short and clear?

answers.a1: Passengers already know every procedure
answers.a2: Long technical explanations are always faster
answers.a3: Stress and noise can make communication harder
answers.a4: Clarity matters only during normal service

flightattendant-s5q4.question: A passenger becomes suddenly unwell. What should cabin crew use?

answers.a1: A guessed diagnosis based on appearance alone
answers.a2: Another passenger’s medicine without proper authority
answers.a3: Their training and the airline’s medical assistance procedure
answers.a4: A promise that no assessment is needed

flightattendant-s5q5.question: Why report the location of a cabin hazard precisely?

answers.a1: So the description sounds longer
answers.a2: So every passenger must inspect it
answers.a4: So help can reach the correct place

flightattendant-s5q6.question: A safety instruction is repeated during a noisy event. Why can repetition help?

answers.a1: It proves the first instruction was wrong
answers.a2: It changes the aircraft’s design
answers.a3: Some people may not have heard or understood it
answers.a4: It removes the need for action

flightattendant-s5q7.question: A situation changes while a response is underway. What does the team need?

answers.a1: Only the original description
answers.a2: A new guess from each person independently
answers.a4: Updated information and coordination

flightattendant-s6q1.question: A passenger has a communication need. What is the best starting point?

answers.a1: Give up on explaining the information
answers.a2: Ask which form of support works for them
answers.a4: Address only their companion

flightattendant-s6q2.question: A passenger with hearing difficulty is speaking with you. What can help?

answers.a1: Assume they cannot make decisions
answers.a2: Face them and check their preferred communication method
answers.a4: Speak while facing away

flightattendant-s6q3.question: Before assisting a passenger physically, what is respectful?

answers.a1: Ask what assistance is wanted and follow the applicable procedure
answers.a2: Assume everyone needs the same help
answers.a4: Ask an unrelated passenger to decide

flightattendant-s6q4.question: What is the best approach to an unfamiliar name?

answers.a1: Replace it with a nickname without asking
answers.a2: Ask politely how to pronounce it
answers.a4: Avoid addressing the person

flightattendant-s6q5.question: A passenger needs more time to respond. What is helpful?

answers.a1: Allow time and check understanding without pressure
answers.a2: Treat a pause as refusal
answers.a4: Ask increasingly complex questions rapidly

flightattendant-s6q6.question: A sensitive personal issue is raised. What should the conversation protect?

answers.a1: An opportunity to photograph the discussion
answers.a2: The person’s privacy as far as practical
answers.a3: A public account of the details
answers.a4: The curiosity of nearby passengers

flightattendant-s6q7.question: Why avoid assumptions about someone’s needs based on age alone?

answers.a1: Age tells you every support need
answers.a2: Only younger passengers need explanations
answers.a3: Only older passengers can ask for assistance
answers.a4: People of the same age can have different abilities and preferences

flightattendant-s7q1.question: What does a weather forecast provide?

answers.a1: An informed prediction that must be checked as conditions change
answers.a2: A guarantee of exact future conditions
answers.a4: A replacement for flight planning

answers.a1: Only the runway length
answers.a2: How far suitable objects can be seen and identified
answers.a4: Only the rate of fuel use

flightattendant-s7q3.question: Why can ice on a wing be hazardous?

answers.a1: It makes weight irrelevant
answers.a2: It improves every control response
answers.a3: It always increases lift without drag
answers.a4: It can change airflow and reduce performance

flightattendant-s7q4.question: Which statement about thunderstorms is sound?

answers.a1: They are harmless without visible lightning
answers.a2: They affect aircraft only on the ground
answers.a3: They can contain several serious aviation hazards
answers.a4: They guarantee smooth air beneath them

answers.a1: Wind with a component across the direction of travel
answers.a2: Wind that always matches the aircraft’s heading
answers.a4: Wind blowing only vertically

answers.a1: A change in the aircraft registration
answers.a2: A guaranteed engine failure
answers.a4: Irregular air movement that can disturb an aircraft’s motion

answers.a1: A change in wind speed or direction over a short distance
answers.a2: The temperature at which metal melts
answers.a4: A change in the aircraft’s paint

flightattendant-s8q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

answers.a1: One third
answers.a2: One quarter
answers.a4: Three quarters

flightattendant-s8q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

flightattendant-s8q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

flightattendant-s8q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

flightattendant-s8q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

answers.a1: 3 m

flightattendant-s8q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

answers.a1: 35 kg
answers.a2: 45 kg
answers.a4: 48 kg

flightattendant-s8q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

flightattendant-s9q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Check each account against other reliable information
answers.a2: Choose the more confident speaker automatically
answers.a3: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a4: Delete both accounts without checking

flightattendant-s9q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a2: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a3: The person left the room at 14:10
answers.a4: The person left because they were guilty

flightattendant-s9q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a1: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion
answers.a2: Its origin and context
answers.a4: Whether its colours are attractive

flightattendant-s9q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a1: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations
answers.a2: Proof that no further checking is needed
answers.a4: Proof that the claim is accurate

flightattendant-s9q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a1: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a2: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor
answers.a3: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: No authorised visitors have passes

flightattendant-s9q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a1: Change the fact to fit the explanation
answers.a2: Reconsider the explanation
answers.a4: Treat your first idea as unchangeable

flightattendant-s9q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a1: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a2: No; earlier events can never cause later ones
answers.a4: Yes; sequence always proves cause

flightattendant-s10q1.question: Why use a checklist rather than memory alone?

answers.a1: To avoid monitoring conditions
answers.a2: To replace training entirely
answers.a3: To support consistent completion of required steps
answers.a4: To guarantee equipment never fails

answers.a1: Watching one instrument and ignoring everything else
answers.a2: Knowing only the destination name
answers.a4: Understanding relevant conditions and how they may develop

flightattendant-s10q3.question: A plan relied on conditions that have now changed. What is needed?

answers.a1: Use the oldest available information
answers.a2: Reassess the plan using current information
answers.a3: Ignore the change if arrival is important
answers.a4: Continue only because time has already been spent

flightattendant-s10q4.question: Why is fatigue relevant to aviation decisions?

answers.a1: It affects only passengers
answers.a2: It removes the need for rest
answers.a4: It can impair attention and judgement

flightattendant-s10q5.question: A strong desire to arrive is influencing a safety decision. What should take priority?

answers.a1: The actual conditions and applicable operating limits
answers.a2: The original promise regardless of conditions
answers.a4: The amount already paid for the trip

flightattendant-s10q6.question: A warning conflicts with an apparently normal indication. What is the sound approach?

answers.a1: Choose whichever indication is more reassuring
answers.a2: Cover the warning to reduce distraction
answers.a3: Use the applicable procedure to assess the discrepancy
answers.a4: Assume warnings can never be correct

flightattendant-s10q7.question: Why keep alternatives in a flight plan?

answers.a1: Conditions may require a change of plan
answers.a2: They make fuel planning unnecessary
answers.a4: A planned destination is always unavailable
